newsitem.title: UK: NWE spot naphtha weaker, paper slower to follow.
newsitem.headline: NWE spot naphtha weaker, paper slower to follow.

text.p: European spot naphtha prices weakened on Wednesday but forward price indicators swaps were relatively stable reflecting sentiment for an eventual boost to naphtha from seasonal gasoline demand, traders said.

Scarce prompt buyers saw physical prices drifting lower and arbitrage options are closing with recent shipments from Europe starting to pressure Asian prices. But while the spot market has weakened, forward paper swaps have been slower to follow.

The April/May contango on swaps widened slightly as April contracts softened and May steadied. traders said this could reflect the anticipated kick-in of the U.S. driving season which usually brings a sharp increase in gasoline demand.
On the spot market trade house selling saw open spec cargoes offered down to around $191 cif NWE.
Despite slack prompt gasoline activity interest was seen for N+A material into the U.K. with a cargo reported traded on Tuesday at mean of cif quotes -$1 per tonne to a U.K. refiner.

Around 400,000 tonnes of naphtha is estimated to have sailed East from Europe. Around half of this has been taken up by short covering into increased petrochemical demand while the balance remains unsold and is starting to pressure prices in Asian.

Asian prices were valued around $230 a tonne on Monday but had already shed around $6 by this morning. Traders said that with relatively expensive freight at around $30 a tonne the arbitrage was no longer profitable.
In the Mediterranean several stems were being shown by trade houses, but traders said the dearth of buying interest at the moment meant levels were hard to pin down.
